name: Chapter / Digital Exercises / Exercises

toolVerdict.whyItTies: The tool compares COLOUR tokens only - 10 of the 44 SLDS-vocabulary tokens this design binds. bingel-dc and bingel-int are colour-identical, so colour cannot separate them and the tool correctly refuses to pick.

theme.familyIsolation: Not in doubt. 7 colour tokens the design binds match exactly 2 of 16 themes, and in every case the pair is {bingel-dc, bingel-int}; no other theme matches any of them: color/foreground/bold #1b1c1e, color/foreground/plain #373a3e, color/background/primary/interactive/plain #0074df, color/foreground/disabled #b8c0c8, color/border/plain #d5d9de, color/background/input/interactive #c7cdd3, color/border/input #8d959d. The rendered frame also carries the Bingel wordmark and 'Uitgeverij VAN IN' (Bingel is VAN IN's platform).

tieBreakBasis.note: The two themes differ in 22 properties and most are font families, but THREE of the 22 are size tokens - and those three are exactly the ones this design binds. bingel-dc matches 0 of 3; bingel-int matches 3 of 3. This is reproducible, not a coin flip.
tieBreakBasis.secondaryAxisAgrees: The font axis points the same way: the design binds text-new/typeset/fontFamily/body = 'Proxima Nova'; bingel-int's brand layer declares 'proxima-nova', bingel-dc's declares 'open-sans'. Both available discriminating axes select bingel-int.
tieBreakBasis.dissentingEvidence: The file contains an effect style literally NAMED 'bingel_dc_shadow' (#0E4F9547, 0 4 12 0). It is a local style name, not a bound SLDS variable, and its colour matches no theme token. The design-analyst treated it as decisive and concluded bingel-dc; three of that same manifest's own numeric rows contradict that conclusion.

theme.siblingDisagreement: A7, a different frame of the SAME Figma file, picked bingel-dc from the same tie. Recorded as a disagreement rather than reconciled. The per-file theme hypothesis is NOT confirmed by these two runs: both agree the file is Bingel, and they split on dc-vs-int. A7's defs tie 15/15 on colour; if A7's frame binds size/borderRadius/* or size/borderWidth/action, the same 3-token test would settle it the same way, and that is the cheap way to reconcile us.
theme.pixelRiskIfWrong: Low. In CSS the two themes differ only in border-radius (4 vs 2px) and action border-width (1 vs 2px); the font-family difference is inert (see fontFamilyDeadToken).
theme.fontFamilyDeadToken: DESIGN-SYSTEM DEFECT: --sl-brand-text-new-*-fontFamily is declared in both Bingel themes (open-sans vs proxima-nova) but NOTHING consumes it - the core block hardcodes --sl-text-new-*-fontFamily: 'Open Sans' at theme.css:3655-3690 and no later declaration maps the brand value in. bingel-int therefore RENDERS Open Sans despite its brand being Proxima Nova, and the two themes are font-identical in practice.
theme.dataUserGroupCheck: Checked for the gated-token trap: bingel-int declares typography under [data-user-group='early'|'developing'|'advanced'], but 0 tokens are declared ONLY there - each also has a plain body declaration. The trap does not bite this theme.
theme.checkTokensUnderBothThemes: check-tokens.mjs is clean under BOTH bingel-dc and bingel-int (0 missing), confirming the two are token-NAME identical; the choice changes resolved values only.

referenceScreenshot.canvasBleed: none - the documented ~8px bleed did NOT occur on this node
referenceScreenshot.newDefect: The reference is uniformly 50% darkened: the MAXIMUM channel value anywhere in the 1,474,560-pixel image is 128. Verified by reconstruction - 128 -> #FFFFFF, #00305D -> #0060B9 (= the design's own color/palette/primary/500 #0060B9), #001325 -> #00264A (= foreground #002649), #797A7B -> #F2F4F6 (= color/palette/neutral/50 #F2F3F5). Cause: the frame's last child is <boolean-operation id='25124:57189' name='Subtract' x='664' y='704' width='0' height='0'/>, a degenerate full-canvas dim layer that get_screenshot composites into the raster. Normalised copy written to reference-normalised.png (v*255/128, clamped). Every colour comparison in this run uses the normalised image; the 50% quantisation means recovered values are even-valued and accurate to +/-1.
referenceScreenshot.correctionToCoordinator: The coordinator's instruction said to normalise 'the ~8px canvas bleed'. This node has NO canvas bleed - get_screenshot returned exactly 1440x1024. The defect here is different and larger: the whole raster is 50% darkened (max channel 128). Both defects exist in this pipeline; they are not the same one.

4-validate.firstAttemptBlocked: The first capture returned nothing-rendered with 404s on two modules that existed on disk. Root cause was NOT the dev server: backticks inside HTML comments within a lit html`` template terminate the template literal, so 4 files were unparseable. esbuild named it; tsc would have too, but the Stage 3 gate was blind (see findings). 7 comment lines across 4 files fixed.
measuredFixes: ONE cause, THREE deltas: a shadow root does not inherit a page-level border-box reset, so every inline-size/block-size was added to its own padding. app bar 56 declared + 12 + 12 = 80 measured; app bar inner 1440 + 24 + 24 = 1488 measured = the exact 48px of document overflow; side nav 240 + 24 + 24 = 288 measured. Fixed at the cause (box-sizing: border-box) rather than by subtracting constants. After: app bar 56, quick bar 40, side nav 240, document scrollWidth 1440 - all exact.

Avatar circles measured 32px against the drawn 40px. Cause: sl-avatar size='md' resolves to --sl-size-400 (32px); size='lg' resolves to --sl-size-500 (40px). The overflow '+2' circle was already hardcoded at 40, so the stack was visibly inconsistent in the first capture. Changed to size='lg'; now 40 exactly.

Chapter header card measured 307px tall against the drawn 232. Cause: the divider and the authorship clusters were stacked BELOW the cover; the Figma frame puts them INSIDE the right-hand column beside it (Frame 467 is 1120x208 and holds the 156x208 cover beside Frame 15495 at 948x208, which itself contains the title block, the divider and the clusters). 208 + 16 + 1 + 16 + 66 = 307, the measured value. Restructured; now 234 (232 content + the card's own 1px top and bottom border).

5-author.scope: An examples/ path, so per the pipeline skill Stage 5 is story enrichment ONLY - no Vitest spec, no website docs, no changeset, no yarn extract-i18n (i18n is off and extract-i18n writes shared files, which this batch forbids).
5-author.note: All five render (verdict 'rendered'). AllAdded shows 63 custom elements against Basic's 59 - the four check-solid icons of the added state, confirming the variant actually exercises the state rather than re-rendering Basic.

criticalFindings: C1 The root page wired ZERO event listeners. Every leaf correctly emitted, so a leaf-level 'does it wire a handler' check passed, but nothing listened: clicking a chapter never expanded it, the nav selection never moved, the add toggle never flipped. This is precisely the failure mode pipeline-defects.md describes as invisible to pixels and the DOM. FIXED: the root now holds a @state() working copy and handles nav-select, chapter-toggle, tool-select, exercise-add-toggle and level-change by mutating it, with documented no-op handlers for the four events that have no drawn state.

C2 Breadcrumbs set no-home and hand-rolled the first crumb, dropping the home glyph. sl-breadcrumbs renders its own <sl-icon name='home-blank'>, and home-blank IS one of the 34 names bingel-int registers - so this run omitted an icon that was available. FIXED: no-home removed, home-url set, only the trailing crumb slotted.

C3 The selected chapter leaf had its two surfaces INVERTED against the design, and the orchestrator's own IMPL-BRIEF had told the implementer to do it that way. Verified pixel by pixel on reference-normalised.png: row interior #FFFFFF (x=300..560,y=765), top border #0060B9 (y=744), left border #0060B9 (x=276), badge #ABD1F5 ground with #004E93 text (x=590..604). FIXED: white row with a full blue-500 border and the light-blue pill on the badge.

C4 All four exercise rows carry the same title, so 'Preview <title>' produced eight identically-named buttons. FIXED: position/total threaded onto the model; labels now read 'Preview exercise 1 of 4: ...'.
minorFindings: M1 Comment in avatar-cluster.css named size='md' where the code correctly uses size='lg'. FIXED (comment only).
M2 sl-search-field's own clear button emits sl-clear, never sl-change, so clearing the field silently produced no event. FIXED by also listening to sl-clear.
M3 Two handlers typed as (event: Event & { detail?: unknown }) rather than importing SlSearchEvent / SlChangeEvent<string>. NOT fixed - carried as a PR comment; runtime behaviour is correct.
M4 ESLint could not run in this environment: 'Cannot find package eslint-plugin-lit' from tools/eslint-plugin-slds. Environment gap, not a code defect; lint is unverified for this run.
